item.title: Bone Loss: A Silent Disease
item.description: About half of women over the age of 50 experience bone density loss, but most don't even know they have a problem. That's why Dr. Jocelyn Wittstein calls it a "silent disease." Dr. Wittstein has been at the forefront of understanding how joint pain and joint health evolve over a woman's lifetime. She tells Norah how you can reverse bone loss and what impact hormones have on bone density.

item.title: Hurricane Polo is a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Polo intensified rapidly in the Pacific off the southwestern Mexican coast, growing into a Category 5 storm before weakening slightly to a Category 4. Here's the latest on its path.

item.title: Nolan Wells' family calls for justice after grand jury declines charges
item.description: An attorney for the family of Mississippi teen Nolan Wells is calling for the Department of Justice to step in after a grand jury declined to charge anyone in his drowning death. CBS News' Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Key takeaways from Trump's day at the U.N. General Assembly
item.description: President Trump touted a "useful" meeting between U.S. and Iranian officials hours after threatening to "annihilate" the nation during his speech at the United Nations General Assembly. Meanwhile, he's set to host Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Many Americans are relying on multiple forms of credit to cover expenses. When is it a warning sign?
item.description: Using several types of credit isn't always a problem, but certain patterns signal that your debt is unsustainable.

item.title: DOJ defends Trump media ban, citing national security and "professionalism"
item.description: The Justice Department claimed that reporting from CNN, MS NOW and Politico raises national security concerns and accused their journalists of failing to act with "professionalism and decorum."

item.title: Diesel prices just hit a new record. Would a U.S. export ban bring relief?
item.description: Some lawmakers want to halt U.S. diesel exports as prices top $6.50 a gallon. But such a ban could have unintended consequences, experts say.

item.title: Eye Opener: Powerful storms threaten millions
item.description: Storms are threatening millions along the East Coast. Meanwhile, Hurricane Polo churns near the West Coast. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: U.S., Iran hold first talks since June as Trump threatens annihilation
item.description: U.S. and Iranian delegations met on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly, rekindling diplomacy amid Trump's threat to "annihilate" the regime.

item.title: Ukraine ready to sign landmark drone defense deal with U.S., sources say
item.description: Sources tell CBS News that Ukraine is ready to sign a landmark drone defense deal with the U.S., as new details of Ukrainian technology helping defend U.S. bases in the Middle East come to light.

item.title: Zelenskyy seeks Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire, U.S. drones deal details emerge
item.description: President Trump spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy about the war with Russia in a meeting at the United Nations General Assembly. Zelenskyy is seeking an energy truce with Russia, and there are new details on a drone defense deal with the U.S. CBS News international reporter Aidan Stretch has more details.

item.title: Why Greenland and Denmark agreed to a deal with Trump
item.description: President Trump signed a new deal with Denmark and Greenland, which would allow the U.S. to open two new military bases in the Arctic. CBS News' Holly Williams has more on this.

item.title: Wife of scholar detained in China wants Trump to press Xi to release him
item.description: Min Zin, a Myanmar scholar, has been held for more than 100 days at what human rights groups say is a "black site" in China.

item.title: Wife of American detained in China holds out hope for his return amid Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: The wife of a U.S. citizen wrongfully detained in China has not spoken with him for more than 100 days. Sylvia Zin spoke with Margaret Brennan, saying she hopes President Trump pushes Chinese President Xi Jinping to release her husband.

item.title: Key moments from the first day of the United Nations General Assembly
item.description: World leaders are gathering at the United Nations General Assembly while the U.S. war in Iran continues. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi and Holly Williams have the latest headlines.

item.title: What is an "AI swarm," and why is it giving tech experts nightmares?
item.description: AI "agents" show a remarkable ability to share information and knowledge with other bots. That should worry us.

item.title: Bone health and the "silent disease": 4 things women should know
item.description: In the latest episode of "Healthful," Dr. Jocelyn Wittstein, an orthopedic surgeon at Duke University School of Medicine, discusses what women should know about protecting their bones.

item.title: Ancient wall found under Paris hotel could confirm origins of city
item.description: The wall dating from the Gallo-Roman period was discovered beneath a hotel on the Ile de la Cite, a stone's throw from Notre Dame Cathedral.

item.title: Venezuela blocks 3 attempts by opposition leader Machado to return, team says
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado tried 3 times to enter her country "by air and sea but has been turned away each time," her team says.

item.title: Redrawn Missouri congressional map lands before Supreme Court for third time
item.description: The fight over Missouri's congressional map returned to the U.S. Supreme Court for a third time after an appeals court ordered the revival of new districts backed by President Trump​.

item.title: Iran's president in N.Y. as Trump weighs cutting deal or driving Iran "into hell"
item.description: President Trump told the U.N. he's deciding whether to make a deal or drive Iran "into hell." Iran's president is slated to address the world body today, Iranian state media say.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue to restore White House access
item.description: The three news organizations, which were banned from White House grounds by President Trump, are arguing that the ban is unconstitutional.

item.title: U.S. to welcome up to 17,500 more White South Africans as refugees
item.description: The Trump administration is planning to welcome up to 17,500 additional White Afrikaners from South Africa as refugees over the next 12 months, according to a notice sent to Congress.

item.title: Have an Apple iPhone 15 or 16? How to file a claim for up to $95.
item.description: The claims window is open until Dec. 21, 2026. To file a claim, iPhone users must enter basic personal info and their iPhone's serial number.

item.title: "Pictures to hurt you": A war photographer's final testament to Vietnam
item.description: "I want my pictures to hurt," British war photographer Sir Don McCullin told CBS News ahead of the publication of his final book: "Vietnam."

item.title: Lack of child care costs families, business and taxpayers $122 billion: study
item.description: 1 in 4 parents has had to quit a job because of child care problems, according to the study.

item.title: Community contributes to girl's "visual bucket list" before she loses her sight
item.description: A story about a little girl who would possibly lose her eyesight had a ripple effect in the community she lived in — and beyond.

item.title: Virginia zoo welcomes rare hippopotamus
item.description: This is the second pygmy hippo calf born at the zoo and in the state of Virginia.

item.title: Yoga group allegedly forced members into sexual exploitation as "geishas"
item.description: The group, which did not offer yoga classes, is accused of trying to lure powerful and wealthy men like opera star Placido Domingo.

item.title: Americans have range of views on timing, circumstances of legal abortions
item.description: Many who oppose legal abortion admit there should be exceptions, while many in favor would set time limits.
